convertibility_reason: Heavy pending order management with time-based placement and deletion cycles. Pending orders are placed at a fixed hour and deleted at closing hour. Position management closes based on time or TP. Requires precise time-of-day order lifecycle management (place stops, delete unfilled orders, close positions on schedule) that is inherently broker-time-dependent and pending-order-centric, making it MT5-only for reliable backtesting and execution.

derived_values.name: ExtDistance

derived_values.name: ExtStopLoss
derived_values.used_by: SL price for SellStop and BuyStop orders

derived_values.name: ExtTakeProfit
derived_values.used_by: Position close condition in PosManager (close when unrealized profit >= ExtTakeProfit)

params.note: TP is checked in PosManager as price distance reached, not set on the pending order itself

other_exits: Position closed when time_struct.hour equals InpClosingHour (time-based forced exit)
All pending orders deleted when time_struct.hour equals InpClosingHour
Buy position closed when (current_price - open_price) >= ExtTakeProfit
Sell position closed when (open_price - current_price) >= ExtTakeProfit

custom_logic_notes: At the opening hour (default 09:00), the EA places BOTH a SellStop and BuyStop simultaneously - a symmetric straddle pattern. SellStop at Bid - Distance, with SL at SellStop price + ExtStopLoss. BuyStop at Ask + Distance, with SL at BuyStop price - ExtStopLoss. Neither pending order has a TP price set; instead TP is enforced in PosManager which monitors open positions and closes them when unrealized profit in pips exceeds InpTakeProfit. At closing hour (default 02:00), all pending orders are deleted and all open positions are force-closed. The timeframe must be <= H1 (enforced in OnInit). The EA uses magic number filtering for both position and order management.
python_conversion_notes: Time-of-day breakout strategy placing symmetric stop orders. Key challenges: (1) Pending order lifecycle - place at opening hour, delete unfilled at closing hour - requires limit/stop order management. (2) Position close on TP distance condition rather than TP price on order - needs runtime position monitoring. (3) Time filtering with hour wraparound (closing hour 02:00 < opening hour 09:00 implies next-day close). (4) No indicators - pure time + price distance logic, so indicator conversion is trivial. (5) Must implement pending order placement and deletion logic. (6) Digit adjustment for 3/5 digit brokers must be replicated. (7) New bar detection logic needed for on_bar equivalent.
